method: exp05c: the LLM (Claude, multimodal) reviewed a 42-frame keyframe grid (1 frame / 20 s, timestamped) plus the 18 stills chosen in exp08, against the subtitle-only understanding (tos_understanding.json). Each item is a fact the subtitles could not provide or got wrong.

corrections.evidence: on-screen intertitle '40 YEARS LATER' (exp08 still for c01-b3)
corrections.fix: There is a 40-year time jump between the breakup and the mission.

corrections.evidence: the man being coached and delivering the final lines is grey-haired
corrections.fix: Present-day Thom is an old man; the young couple on the bridge in the present is a re-creation of the past.

corrections.evidence: giant robots fight in the city; a colossal robot head faces old Thom
corrections.fix: Celia's threat is literal: she commands/is a giant robot; Thom's old nightmare about 'giant robotic claws' pays off.

corrections.evidence: Amsterdam canals/bridge; foggy ruined future city with floating ships seen through a scope; ruined church
corrections.fix: Setting: Amsterdam, then a devastated future Amsterdam.

corrections.evidence: a heavy man with a cybernetic eye implant runs the operation from a cluttered room, with a woman soldier
corrections.fix: The 'director' is a cyborg-eyed operator; he also delivers the closing 'could'a gone worse'.
Mark 09:45-end as credits: exclude from clip/still candidates.

corrections.evidence: burned-in Chinese subtitles at the bottom of the frame
corrections.fix: This release carries foreign hardsubs: penalize/crop frames with burned-in text for stills; keep using the English SRT for meaning.

corrections.evidence: young Thom and young Celia on the bridge, robot claw at Thom's face, Celia furious
corrections.fix: Subtitle-only reading of the re-staged breakup and Celia's anger was correct.

beat_audit.notes: Plot spine (breakup -> re-staging to overwrite memory -> heartbreak -> apology -> reconciliation) was right from subtitles alone; errors were in WHO (age), WHAT FORM (giant robot), WHEN (40-year jump), WHERE (Amsterdam) and STRUCTURE (credits). These are exactly the facts a recap narrator needs to say on screen, so a cheap visual pass is required for faithful narration.
